No. 6 of 2025
AN ACT to amend the Criminal Code, Cap. 3.01.
[ 31st March, 2025 ]
BE IT ENACTED by the King’s Most Excellent Majesty, by
and with the advice and consent of the House of Assembly and the
Senate of Saint Lucia, and by the authority of the same, as follows:

80
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
Short title
1. This Act may be cited as the Criminal Code (Amendment)
Act, 2025.
Interpretation
2. In this Act, “principal Act” means the Criminal Code, Cap. 3.01.
Amendment of section 774
3. Section 774 of the principal Act is amended, in subsection
(7), by inserting immediately after the word “jury” the words “or
judge alone”.
Amendment of section 873
4. Section 873 of the principal Act is amended by deleting the
word “magistrate” and by substituting the words “a master or judge”.
Substitution of section 874
5. The principal Act is amended by deleting section 874 and by
substituting the following —
“Trial by judge and jury or judge alone
874. A person against whom an indictment is filed shall,
subject to this Act, be tried by judge and jury as constituted
in accordance with this Act, unless —
(a) he or she elects to be tried by a judge alone in
accordance with section 874A(1) and the Criminal
Procedure Rules, Cap. 3.01;
(b) the prosecution makes an application to the court
for a trial by judge alone on the grounds specified
under section 874A(2) and in accordance with the
Criminal Procedure Rules, Cap. 3.01;
(c) a judge in a trial by judge and jury makes an order
under section 974A(3)(a) or 974A(5).”.

81
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
Insertion of new section 874A
6. The prinicpal Act is amended by inserting immediately after
section 874 the following new section 874A —
“Application of trial by judge alone
874A.—(1) An accused person may make an election for a
trial by judge alone where an indictment has been filed against
him or her and the trial has not commenced under this Act or
another enactment.”.
(2) The prosecution may make an application for a trial by a
judge alone to the court, where an indictment has been
filed against an accused person and the trial has not
commenced, on the following grounds —
(a) that in view of the nature and circumstances of the
case —
(i) there is a danger of jury tampering or intimidation
of witnesses,
(ii) a material witness is afraid or unwilling to give
evidence before a jury,
(b) there is a likelihood that, if a jury is selected, pre-trial
publicity may influence the decision of the Court;
(c) that the case involves a criminal gang element and
would be properly tried without a jury;
(d) that the complexity of the trial or the length of the
trial, or both, is likely to make the trial so burdensome
to the jury that the interest of justice requires the trial
to be conducted without a jury.
(3) An election under subsection (1) and an application under
subsection (2) shall be heard and determined in the absence
of a jury and the prosecution and the accused person
shall be given an opportunity to make representation with
respect to the election or application for a trial by judge
alone.

82
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
(4) If the judge is satisfied that a ground as specified under
subsection (2) is established, he or she shall make an order
that the trial be conducted without a jury, including any
preliminary issue of fitness to plead or stand trial.
(5) If the judge is satisfied that a ground as specified under
subsection (2) is not established, he or she shall refuse
the application for a trial by judge alone.
(6) An appeal does not not lie against an order of the judge
to grant or refuse an application for a trial by judge alone
under subsection (2).
(7) In subsection (2)(a)(i), a “danger of jury tampering or
intimidation of witnesses” includes an instance where —
(a) there is a threat or actual harm to, or intimidate or
bribe a juror, witness, or any family member of that
juror or witness;
(b) there is a threat or actual harm to the property of a
juror, witness or a family member of that juror or
witness;
(c) the trial is a retrial and the jury in the previous trial was
discharged because of jury tampering or intimidation
of a witness;
(d) jury tampering or intimidation of a witness has taken
place in previous criminal proceedings involving the
accused person or any of the accused;
(e) there has been intimidation, attempted intimidation of
a person who is likely to be a witness in the trial.”.
Substitution of section 892
7. The principal Act is amended by deleting section 892 and by
substituting the following —
“Jury or judge alone to find if accused capable to plead for trial
892.—(1) In the case of a judge alone trial or where the
attorneys-at-law agree, and the accused person is called on to
plead to the indictment, if it appears to be uncertain for any

83
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
reason whether the accused person is capable of understanding
the proceedings at the trial so as to be able to make a proper
defence, the judge alone may find, by the written or oral
evidence of a medical practitioner, whether or not the accused
person is so capable.
(2) In the case of a trial by judge and jury and where the
attorneys-at-law have a difference of opinion on the capability
of an accused person to understand the proceedings at the trial
so as to be able to make a proper defence, a jury chosen
from the panel of jurors shall be empanelled immediately and
shall be sworn, to find whether or not the accused person is
so capable.
(3) Where the judge alone under subsection (1) or the jury under
subsection (2) finds the accused person to be capable of
understanding the proceedings, the trial shall proceed.
(4) Where the judge alone under subsection (1) or the jury under
subsection (2) finds the accused person is not capable of
understanding the proceedings at the trial so as to be able
to make a proper defence, the finding shall be recorded
and the Court may order the accused person to be discharged
or may order him or her to be kept in custody in a place and
manner as the Court thinks fit until he or she is dealt with
according to law.
(5) An accused person found to be incapable of understanding the
proceedings at the trial, may subsequently be indicted and tried
for the offence if he or she is found capable of understanding
the proceedings.”.
Amendment of section 921
8. The principal Act is amended by deleting section 921 and by
substituting the following —
“Duties and powers of a jury or judge alone
921.—(1) The jury in a trial by judge and jury or the judge alone
in a trial by judge alone shall —
(a) decide which view of the facts is true and return
as he or she determines the verdict which, consistent

84
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
with such view, ought according to the direction
of the judge to be returned in a trial by jury, or
in the case of a trial by judge by judge alone;
(b) determine the meaning of all technical terms
and words used in an unusual sense which it may
be necessary to determine, whether such words
occur in documents or not,
(c) determine all questions which, according to
law, are to be deemed questions of fact,
(d) decide whether general indefinite expressions
apply to a particular case.
(2) The judge in a trial by judge and jury or a trial by judge
alone shall determine —
(a) the meaning of a term of law; and
(b) whether a general indefinite expression applies to a
particular case where —
(i) an expression refers to a legal procedure, or
(ii) the meaning of an expression to be ascertained by
law.”.
Amendment of section 923
9. Section 923 of the principal Act is amended by —
(a) deleting the section heading and by substituting the
following —
“VERDICTS AND REASONS FOR DECISION”;
(b) deleting subsection (3) and by substituting the following —
“(3) The maximum length of time to consider a verdict —
(a) in the case of a trial by judge and jury, for a jury
is six hours;
(b) in the case of a trial by judge alone, for the judge
alone is twenty-four hours.”;

85
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
(c) inserting immediately after subsection (3) the following
new subsections (4), (5), (6), (7) and (8) —
“(4) Where a verdict is delivered on a Friday, the twenty-
four hour period specified under subsection (3)(b) does
not include a Saturday, Sunday or Bank Holiday.
(5) In the case of a trial by judge and jury, the jury shall
deliver the verdict orally.
(6) In the case of a trial by judge alone, the judge alone shall
deliver the verdict orally.
(7) After the case is closed on both sides, a written decision
must be provided to the accused person within seven days
of the oral delivery of the verdict under subsection (6).
(8) A written decision under subsection (7) must specify
—
(a) the reasons for the conviction or acquittal;
(b) the principles of law applied by the judge;
(c) the findings of fact on which the judge relied.”.
Insertion of new sections 974A and 974B
10. The principal Act is amended by inserting immediately after
section 974 the following new sections 974A and 974B—
“Discharge of jury as a result of jury tampering
974A.—(1) This section applies where —
(a) a judge is minded during a trial on indictment
to discharge the jury; and
(b) a judge is so minded to discharge the jury
as jury tampering appears to have taken
place.
(2) Before taking any steps to discharge the jury under
subsection (3), the judge must —
(a) inform the parties that he or she is minded to
discharge the jury;

86
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
(b) inform the parties of the grounds on which he or
she is so minded; and
(c) allow the parties an opportunity to make
representations.
(3) Where the judge, after considering any representations
under subsection (2)(c), discharges the jury, he or she
may make an order to continue the trial by judge alone,
if satisfied that —
(a) jury tampering has taken place; and
(b) subject to subsection (4), the continuation of the
trial without a jury is fair to the defendant.
(4) If the judge considers that it is necessary in the interests
of justice for the trial to be terminated he or she may,
make an order to terminate the trial.
(5) Without prejudice to any other power that the judge
has with respect to terminating a trial, where the judge
terminates a trial under subsection (4), he or she may
make an order that a new trial which is to take place must
be a trial by judge alone if he or she is satisfied in respect
of the new trial that —
(a) it is likely that there is evidence of a real and
present danger that jury tampering would take
place; and
(b) notwithstanding any reasonable steps to prevent
jury tampering, including the provision of police
protection, the likelihood that jury tampering
would take place is so substantial as to make it
necessary in the interests of justice to have a trial
by judge alone.
(6) A real and present danger that jury tampering may
take place where —
(a) the trial is a retrial and the jury in the previous
trial was discharged because jury tampering had
taken place;

87
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
(b) jury tampering has taken place in previous criminal
proceedings involving the defendant;
(c) there has been intimidation, or attempted
intimidation, of any person who is likely to be a
witness in the trial.
Appeals
974B.—(1) An appeal shall lie to the Court of Appeal
at the instance of the accused person, from a decision of
the judge convicting an accused person —
(i) without leave of the judge or Court of Appeal —
(A) that the Court had no jurisdiction in the case;
(B) that the Court exceeded its jurisdiction in the case;
(C) that the Judge was personally interested in the
case;
(D) that the Judge acted corruptly, maliciously or was
biased in the case;
(E) that the decision was obtained by fraud;
(F) that the case has been already heard or tried and
decided by, or forms the subject of a hearing or
trial pending before, some competent court;
(G) that legally admissible evidence substantially
affecting the merits of the case was rejected by
the Court;
(H) that legally inadmissible evidence was admitted
by the Court and that there is not sufficient legal
evidence to sustain the decision after rejecting
such illegal evidence; or
(I) that the decision was erroneous in some other
point of law.
(ii) with leave of the Court of Appeal —
(A) that the decision is unreasonable or cannot be
supported having regard to the evidence;

88
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
(B) that the judgment or sentence passed was based
on a wrong principle or was such that a Court
viewing the circumstances reasonably could not
properly have so decided; or
(C) that the sentence imposed was unduly severe.
(2) An appeal shall lie to the Court of Appeal, at the
instance of the prosecution, from the decision of the judge
acquitting the accused person on any of the following
grounds —
(a) without leave of the Court of Appeal, that the
decision was erroneous on a point of law;
(b) with leave of the Court of Appeal, that the sentence
is manifestly inadequate or is wrong in law.
(3) In the determination of an appeal the Court of Appeal
shall, subject to this Act and the rules of court, have all
the powers of the Court of Appeal under the Eastern
Caribbean Supreme Court Act Cap.143 in relation to
criminal appeals.”.
Insertion of new sections 998A and 998B
11. The principal Act is amended by inserting immediately after
section 998, the following new sections 998A and 998B —
“Jurisdiction of a judge in a trial by judge alone
998A. In a trial by a judge alone, the judge alone has —
(a) the power, authority and jurisdiction which he or she
has in a trial by judge and jury; and
(b) the power to determine a question and to make a
finding which is required to be determined or made
by a jury.
References to jury to be treated as a reference to a judge alone in a
trial by judge alone
998B.—(1) Except where the context otherwise requires, a
reference in this Code or another enactment to a jury,
in the case of the verdict of a jury or the findings of a jury is
a reference to a judge alone in a trial by judge alone.

89
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
(2) This Code or another enactment shall, to the extent that
this Code or another enactment is predicated on a trial by
judge and jury, be construed with such modifications as may
be necessary to be in conformity with a trial by judge alone.”.
Substitution of section 1018
12. The principal Act is amended by deleting section 1018 and
by substituting the following —
“Issue of mentally abnormal on or before arraignment
1018.—(1) Where an accused person appears, on or before
arraignment, to be mentally ill, the Court may, after hearing
evidence in that regard, find whether the accused person is
mentally ill and unfit for his or her trial and the Court
shall, if it finds that the accused person is mentally ill, return
a verdict that the accused person is mentally ill.
(2) A verdict under this section does not affect the trial of
the accused person found to be mentally ill for the offence for
which he or she is indicted, if he or she subsequently
becomes of sound mind.”.
Substitution of section 1019
13. The principal Act is amended by deleting section 1019 and
by substituting the following —
“Special verdict if jury or judge alone finds that accused was
mentally ill at time of offence
1019.—(1) If an accused is charged with an offence, and at the
trial evidence is given that the accused was mentally ill and
not responsible, according to law, for his or her actions at
the time when the act was committed, and, if it appears to
the jury in a trial by judge and jury or the judge alone in a
trial by judge alone that he or she committed the act charged,
the jury or judge alone shall return a special verdict.
(2) A special verdict under subsection (1) must specify
that the accused person is guilty of the act with which he
or she is charged but was mentally ill at the time when he or she
committed the act.”.

90
No. 6 ] Criminal Code (Amendment) Act [ 2025
Amendment of section 1020
14. Section 1020 of the principal Act is amended by —
(a) deleting the section heading and by substituting the
following —
“Person found mentally ill may be detained”;
(b) inserting immediately after the word “jury”, wherever it
appears, the words “or of the judge in a trial by judge
alone”.
Passed in the House of Assembly this 11th day of March, 2025.
CLAUDIUS J. FRANCIS,
Speaker of the House of Assembly.
Passed in the Senate this 18th day of March, 2025.
ALVINA REYNOLDS,
President of the Senate.
SAINT LUCIA
